ev.q: bivalent boosters provided significant additional protection against symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection
Relative vaccine effectiveness (rVE) of a bivalent booster dose compared with that of ≥2 monovalent vaccine doses
rVE increased with time since the most recent monovalent vaccine dose in all age groups
Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using multivariable logistic regression
case-patients were persons who received a positive rapid or laboratory-based NAAT result; control-patients were those who received a negative NAAT result
This study evaluated aVE and rVE by number of previous monovalent doses received

methods_quotes.q: Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using multivariable logistic regression
rVE was calculated by comparing the odds of receiving a bivalent booster dose (after 2, 3, or 4 monovalent doses) versus not receiving
Multivariable logistic regression models were controlled for age, gender, race, ethnicity, SVI of the testing location
VE estimates with 95% CIs >50 percentage points are not shown because of imprecision.
